Finalize then ranks from the graph instead of `GetWhereUsed`, which returns 404 on ECC.
4	
5	`<DIR>` = the inventory directory from the `WALKED` line. `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` = the folder that holds `skills/`, `scripts/`, `common/` (two levels above this skill's `SKILL.md`, or `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`); quote it in shell commands. `<SAPV>` = `ECC` or `S4` as in `stocker-fanout.md`.
6	
7	Banner: `▶ phase=graph · agent=main · batch reads`. Every sub-step is mechanical — no judgment, so no Sonnet / Opus dispatch here. G1, G1b and G3a run as **batch reads on the main thread**: `scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs` writes the plan, `scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs` runs it in one process (read tools only; DD-shaped `GetSqlQuery` only) and prints one line per call — `<id>⇥OK⇥<value>` or `<id>⇥ERROR⇥<message>`. Results stay on disk; never Read the sources or the SQL results. Batch fallback: when `sap-batch` fails as a whole (`sap-batch: <error>`, exit ≠ 0 — the bridge did not start), print `↳ batch reads unavailable: <error>` and run the same scope with `sc4sap:sap-checker` (`MODE: scout`, 10 objects per checker, at most 8 per message, one line per object `key="src" value="<folder>"` / `value="ERROR <message>"`, never read the source).
8	
9	## G1 — Fetch sources (main thread, batch)
10	
11	Scope = every `PROG/P` and `FUGR` in `walk.json → objects[]` (`PROG/I` members are includes: read through their owner, or in G1b). `calls` = 0 → skip.
12	
13	```bash
14	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --sources "<DIR>/walk.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-src.json"
15	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-src.json"
16	```
17	
18	Callers that keep sources between runs add `--skip-present "<SRC>"` to the first command (member folders already on disk are not fetched again). More than 150 calls → run the plan in parts, `--from 1 --to 150`, `--from 151 --to 300`, … (one Bash call each; a part takes about two minutes). `OK` lines carry the member folder (`GetProgFullCode` `output: "file"`, ends in `.prog` / `.fugr`). `<SRC>` = their parent directory (one MCP output directory). `ERROR` lines are not retried — `build-package-graph` lists those objects under `sourcesMissing`, and finalize names them in `index.md`.
19	
20	### G1b — Includes no member program pulls in
21	
22	Package includes no G1 folder holds: user-exit includes (included by SAP programs such as `MV45AFZZ`), leftovers, and includes a member program pulls in that its `GetProgFullCode` folder came back without:
23	
24	```bash
25	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/build-package-graph.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --src "<SRC>" --orphans > "<DIR>/orphans.json"
26	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --orphans "<DIR>/orphans.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-incl.json"
27	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-incl.json"
28	```
29	
30	`calls` = 0 → skip the last command. The files land in `<SRC>` as `<name>.incl.abap`. G5 joins an include to the member program whose source has `INCLUDE <name>`; the others become objects of their own. Its summary reports what is still missing under `orphanIncludes`.
31	
32	## G2 — TCodes (main thread)
33	
34	TRAN members → one `GetTransaction` call with `transaction_names: [...]` (batches of 100). Save the JSON result unchanged as `<DIR>/tcodes.json`. It maps report / dialog TCodes to their program and parameter TCodes (SM30) to their view. A failed call → write `[]` and add `TCode mapping unavailable: <message>` to the finalize prompt.
35	
36	## G3 — DDIC relations
37	
38	Two ways in. G3a reads the DD repository tables once per table kind. G3b is the per-object checker read: it is the fallback for what G3a could not read, and the only way for callers that do not allow `GetSqlQuery` (`module-to-process`). Edge kinds: `types` (field → DTEL, `.INCLUDE` / `.APPEND` → STRU, DTEL → DOMA), `checks` (field → check table, with cardinality), `searchHelp`, `valueTable`, `rowType`, `basedOn` (view → base table), `selects` (search help → selection method), `contains` (collective search help). Only customer (Z / Y / namespace) targets and members become nodes.
39	
40	### G3a — DD reads (main thread, batch; stock-cbo only)
41	
42	The one exception to "no `GetSqlQuery`" in this skill: **DD\* repository tables and repository short-text tables only** — the statements in the plan file, nothing else, never `acknowledge_risk`. They are metadata about the package's DDIC objects, never business rows. The `permission-approver` hook auto-approves these statements (`output: "file"` is part of the match — never drop it); any other form prompts. Neither the SQL text nor the results pass through the main thread.
43	
44	```bash
45	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --lang <SAP_LANGUAGE> --out "<DIR>/ddic-plan.json"
46	```
47	
48	It writes the plan (DD03L, DD08L, DD05S, DD35L, DD04L, DD01L, DD40L, DD26S, DD30L, DD31S — single-table `SELECT … WHERE … IN (…)`; S4 packs 200 names per statement, ECC 50 because the `TABLE_READ` condition travels in a URL), plus the object short texts in the logon language and English (DD02T, DD04T, DD01T, DD40T, DD30T, DD25T, TRDIRT, TSTCT, TFTIT, TLIBT, SEOCLASSTX — repository texts, never business rows; the relation map shows them as descriptions). On ECC, names containing `SELECT` or `JOIN` are left out: `TABLE_READ` refuses any condition with those words, literals included. It prints `{ plan, statements, slices: [{ from, to }] }`. `statements` = 0 → no DDIC members; skip G3. Otherwise run every statement as one batch (`sap-batch` refuses any statement that is not in the DD shape the hook auto-approves):
49	
50	```bash
51	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --ddic "<DIR>/ddic-plan.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-dd.json"
52	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-dd.json"
53	```
54	
55	Batch fallback (see the banner note): one `sap-checker` per slice, `MODE: dd-read`, prompt `Plan file: <DIR>/ddic-plan.json — run entries <from>–<to> (1-based, in order). For each entry call GetSqlQuery { sql_query: <entry.sql>, row_number: <entry.row_number>, output: "file" }.`
56	
57	Then (main thread, one Bash call; `<SQLDIR>` = the `sql` folder of the MCP output directory, next to `<SRC>` — `<PROJECT>/.sc4sap/work/<alias>/mcp-output/sql`):
58	
59	```bash
60	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>"
61	```
62	
63	It matches each plan entry to its result file by exact SQL text and writes `<DIR>/ddic-reads.json` (`{ id, table, path, rows, truncated }` or `{ id, table, error }`), printing `{ reads, ok, errors, truncated }`. Batch `ERROR` lines (or checker `RUN … result=error` lines) are only for the progress line.
64	
65	G3b then covers the gaps: a `dd03l-*` read failed or truncated → the tables of that statement; a `DD04L` / `DD01L` / `DD40L` / `DD26S` read failed → the DTEL / DOMA / TTYP / VIEW members of that statement. A failed `DD08L` / `DD05S` / `DD35L` / `DD30L` / `DD31S` read only loses cardinality or search help detail — no G3b for it. No result file was written (MCP server older than 4.8.19 ignores `output`; a fallback checker reports `result=inline`) → G3b for the whole scope; same when every read failed with the same error — print `↳ G3a DD reads unavailable: <error>`. On ECC an `is not allowed` error means the system's `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` predates the DD allow list (reinstall via `/sc4sap:setup`).
66	
67	### G3b — Per-object reads (`sc4sap:sap-checker` × n, `MODE: scout`)
68	
69	DDIC metadata only (`GetTable` / `GetStructure` / `GetDataElement` / `GetDomain` / `GetTypeInfo`) — never `GetSqlQuery` / `GetTableContents`. Scope = the members G3a did not cover, 20 per checker, at most 8 checkers per message. It can share a message with G1.
70	
71	```
72	MODE: scout
73	Objects (your whole scope): <NAME:TABL, NAME:STRU, NAME:DTEL, NAME:DOMA, NAME:TTYP, …>
74	For each object, one read; lines only for customer targets (name starts with Z or Y, or a /namespace/):
75	- TABL / STRU: GetTable (TABL) or GetStructure (STRU). Per field with a customer rollname or domname:
76	  key="types" value="<FIELDNAME>=<ROLLNAME>/<DOMNAME>" (no domname → "<FIELDNAME>=<ROLLNAME>").
77	  Per customer check table (field checktable, or DDL "with foreign key <TAB>"): key="check" value="<FIELDNAME>=<TAB>".
78	  Per included structure (.INCLUDE / .APPEND row precfield, or DDL "include <STRU>"): key="include" value="<STRU>".
79	  Per field search help (field shlpname, or DDL "with value help <SHLP>"): key="shlp" value="<FIELDNAME>=<SHLP>".
80	- DTEL: GetDataElement → key="domain" value="<DOMNAME or ->"; search help set → key="shlp" value="<SHLP>".
81	- DOMA: GetDomain → value table set → key="valtab" value="<TAB>".
82	- TTYP: S/4 only — GetTypeInfo → row type → key="rowtype" value="<ROWTYPE>". On ECC no line.
83	A field the answer does not have (older ECC bridge) gives no line — never guess.
84	```
85	
86	Main writes every `CHECKER … END` block unchanged to `<DIR>/ddic-facts.md` (malformed block → repair once per `../../common/structured-return-repair.md`). A `BLOCKED` batch is not retried. Its objects then have no DDIC edges, and their DTEL / DOMA show `no-evidence`.
87	
88	`build-package-graph` (G5) merges `ddic-reads.json`, `ddic.json` and `ddic-facts.md`. Its summary line names G3a reads that failed or were truncated (`ddicReads`).
89	
90	## G4 — Usage (main thread, ECC only)
91	
92	`<SAPV>` = `ECC` and the tools exist:
93	
94	- `GetTcodeUsage` with every TRAN member (months 12) → the result as `tcodes`.
95	- `GetJobUsage` with every PROG member (months 12) → the result as `jobs`.
96	
97	Write `<DIR>/usage.json` = `{ "system": <SAP system id>, "measuredAt": <today>, "tcodes": …, "jobs": … }` (results unchanged). Either call fails → leave that key out. S/4 or neither tool available → no `usage.json`. The graph is still built, and finalize skips the usage section.
98	
99	### G4u — Usage from another system (QA / PRD)
100	
101	A DEV profile (`config.json → tier` = `DEV`) measures developer tests, not business use. The destination is site-specific: every installation names its own — never assume one. Read `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST` from the profile `sap.env`.
102	
103	- **Set** → G4 calls `GetTcodeUsage` with `destination: "<SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST>"` (passed explicitly, so a just-edited `sap.env` works without a restart). The result's `system` is the measured SID → write it as `tcodes.source = { system, destination, kind: "rfc" }`. `GetJobUsage` stays on the connected system — say so in the progress line. A call error (`RFC destination … failed`, missing authorization) → print it and fall through to the question below.
104	- **Not set** on a DEV profile → ask once (any SAP version — the file path works on S/4 too): `Read QA / PRD over RFC (Recommended)` / `Submit QA / PRD used TCodes (file)` / `Use <SAP system id> statistics` / `Skip usage`.
105	  - RFC → ask for the SM59 destination name (on the connected system, pointing to QA / PRD); prerequisites: the destination's user needs `S_RFC` for function groups `SWNC_COLLECTOR` + `SRFC` and workload read authorization (`S_TOOLS_EX`). Call once; success → offer to save it as `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST` via `/sc4sap:sap-option` (one line, no auto-write).
106	  - File → the export recipe below.
107	
108	Submitted file: print the export recipe, then take a file path or a pasted list:
109	
110	```
111	QA/PRD → ST03N → Expert mode → Workload: Total → Month (pick the months) → Transaction Profile → Standard
112	→ Transaction tab → List → Export → Spreadsheet (.xlsx) or Local file (unconverted .txt).
113	Or paste TCode names here (any separator). Jobs (optional): SM37 list of program names, same way.
114	Window: how many months does the export cover?
115	```
116	
117	A pasted list → write it to `<DIR>/usage-input-tcodes.txt` (Write tool) first. Then (main thread, one Bash call per kind):
118	
119	```bash
120	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/import-usage.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --file "<file>" --system <QA SID> --months <n> [--kind jobs]
121	```
122	
123	It keeps only package members, sets every member absent from the file to `false`, records `source` (system, file, date), and prints `{ kind, members, used, notInPackage }`. Exit 2 = no package member in the file → show the message, ask once for another file, else continue without usage. `notInPackage` > 0 is normal (other packages' TCodes) — print the count only. Submitted TCodes + live `GetJobUsage` may be combined; the usage result names each source in its caveats. Resume: an imported side (`source.kind` = `user-file`) is reused like a measured one (≤ 7 days).
124	
125	## G5 — Build (main thread, one Bash call)
126	
127	```bash
128	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/build-package-graph.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --src "<SRC>" --system <SAP system id> --sap-version <SAPV>
129	```
130	
131	It prints one JSON line `{ graph, nodes, edges, unresolved, sourcesMissing, usage?, fields? }` and writes `<DIR>/graph.json` (+ `usage-result.json`, `usage.md` when `usage.json` exists; `fields.json` — field-level CRUD for the relation map's Fields tab — when G3a read DD03L). Exit code ≠ 0 → print the stderr line and continue to Step D without a graph (finalize falls back to the scout facts). Do not read the JSON files into the main context. Finalize reads them.
132	
133	Progress line after G5: `↳ G graph <nodes> nodes · <edges> edges · used <direct>+<indirect> · unused <unused>` (+ ` · fields <refs> refs` when `fields` is present).
134	
135	## G6 — Customer appends of standard tables (G3a callers only, after G5)
136	
137	The Fields tab also lists the customer fields appended to the standard tables the package reads or writes (VBAK-ZZ…, CI_ includes). Two small DD03L rounds, same checker contract and hook approval as G3a; skip G6 when G1 parsed no source (no `reads` / `writes` in the graph) or `GetSqlQuery` is not allowed.
138	
139	```bash
140	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --only appends --out "<DIR>/ddic-append-plan.json"
141	# checkers on ddic-append-plan.json (MODE: dd-read) → then:
142	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>" --plan ddic-append-plan.json --out ddic-appends.json
143	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --only append-fields --out "<DIR>/ddic-append-fields-plan.json"
144	# checkers on ddic-append-fields-plan.json → then:
145	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>" --plan ddic-append-fields-plan.json --out ddic-append-fields.json
146	```
147	
148	`statements` = 0 in either round → stop G6 there (no standard table read, or no customer append). Then rerun G5 — it merges both files into `fields.json`. A failed round only loses the append fields; never fall back to G3b for it. Resume: both files ≤ 7 days old are reused.
149	
150	## What finalize does with it
151	
152	Spec: [`../../agents/sap-stocker.md`](../../agents/sap-stocker.md) § Dispatch_Modes → `MODE: finalize`. In short:
153	
154	- `ref_count` per member = incoming edges in `graph.json` from other members, excluding `include` (`graph-query.mjs <graph.json> stats` → `degree[].in`). This replaces `n/a (ECC …)`.
155	- `inventory.json → objects[].usage` = `direct` / `indirect` / `unused` / `no-evidence` from `usage-result.json`. `inventory.json → usage` = `{ window, counts, caveats }`.
156	- `index.md` gets a **Usage** section: counts, the window caveats verbatim, and direct + unused lists. `no-evidence` is never called unused.
157	
158	Resume: `tcodes.json` / `ddic-reads.json` + `ddic-facts.md` / `usage.json` in `<DIR>` that are ≤ 7 days old are reused (skip G2 / G3 / G4). G5 always reruns — it takes seconds.

It writes the plan (DD03L, DD08L, DD05S, DD35L, DD04L, DD01L, DD40L, DD26S, DD30L, DD31S — single-table `SELECT … WHERE … IN (…)`; S4 packs 200 names per statement, ECC 50 because the `TABLE_READ` condition travels in a URL), plus the object short texts in the logon language and English (DD02T, DD04T, DD01T, DD40T, DD30T, DD25T, TRDIRT, TSTCT, TFTIT, TLIBT, SEOCLASSTX — repository texts, never business rows; the relation map shows them as descriptions). On ECC, names containing `SELECT` or `JOIN` are left out: `TABLE_READ` refuses any condition with those words, literals included. It prints `{ plan, statements, slices: [{ from, to }] }`. `statements` = 0 → no DDIC members; skip G3. Otherwise run every statement as one batch (`sap-batch` refuses any statement that is not in the DD shape the hook auto-approves):

```bash
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --ddic "<DIR>/ddic-plan.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-dd.json"
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-dd.json"
```

Batch fallback (see the banner note): one `sap-checker` per slice, `MODE: dd-read`, prompt `Plan file: <DIR>/ddic-plan.json — run entries <from>–<to> (1-based, in order). For each entry call GetSqlQuery { sql_query: <entry.sql>, row_number: <entry.row_number>, output: "file" }.`

Then (main thread, one Bash call; `<SQLDIR>` = the `sql` folder of the MCP output directory, next to `<SRC>` — `<PROJECT>/.sc4sap/work/<alias>/mcp-output/sql`):

```bash
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>"
```

It matches each plan entry to its result file by exact SQL text and writes `<DIR>/ddic-reads.json` (`{ id, table, path, rows, truncated }` or `{ id, table, error }`), printing `{ reads, ok, errors, truncated }`. Batch `ERROR` lines (or checker `RUN … result=error` lines) are only for the progress line.

G3b then covers the gaps: a `dd03l-*` read failed or truncated → the tables of that statement; a `DD04L` / `DD01L` / `DD40L` / `DD26S` read failed → the DTEL / DOMA / TTYP / VIEW members of that statement. A failed `DD08L` / `DD05S` / `DD35L` / `DD30L` / `DD31S` read only loses cardinality or search help detail — no G3b for it. No result file was written (MCP server older than 4.8.19 ignores `output`; a fallback checker reports `result=inline`) → G3b for the whole scope; same when every read failed with the same error — print `↳ G3a DD reads unavailable: <error>`. On ECC an `is not allowed` error means the system's `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` predates the DD allow list (reinstall via `/sc4sap:setup`).

### G3b — Per-object reads (`sc4sap:sap-checker` × n, `MODE: scout`)

DDIC metadata only (`GetTable` / `GetStructure` / `GetDataElement` / `GetDomain` / `GetTypeInfo`) — never `GetSqlQuery` / `GetTableContents`. Scope = the members G3a did not cover, 20 per checker, at most 8 checkers per message. It can share a message with G1.

```
MODE: scout
Objects (your whole scope): <NAME:TABL, NAME:STRU, NAME:DTEL, NAME:DOMA, NAME:TTYP, …>
For each object, one read; lines only for customer targets (name starts with Z or Y, or a /namespace/):
- TABL / STRU: GetTable (TABL) or GetStructure (STRU). Per field with a customer rollname or domname:
  key="types" value="<FIELDNAME>=<ROLLNAME>/<DOMNAME>" (no domname → "<FIELDNAME>=<ROLLNAME>").
  Per customer check table (field checktable, or DDL "with foreign key <TAB>"): key="check" value="<FIELDNAME>=<TAB>".
  Per included structure (.INCLUDE / .APPEND row precfield, or DDL "include <STRU>"): key="include" value="<STRU>".
  Per field search help (field shlpname, or DDL "with value help <SHLP>"): key="shlp" value="<FIELDNAME>=<SHLP>".
- DTEL: GetDataElement → key="domain" value="<DOMNAME or ->"; search help set → key="shlp" value="<SHLP>".
- DOMA: GetDomain → value table set → key="valtab" value="<TAB>".
- TTYP: S/4 only — GetTypeInfo → row type → key="rowtype" value="<ROWTYPE>". On ECC no line.
A field the answer does not have (older ECC bridge) gives no line — never guess.
```

Main writes every `CHECKER … END` block unchanged to `<DIR>/ddic-facts.md` (malformed block → repair once per `../../common/structured-return-repair.md`). A `BLOCKED` batch is not retried. Its objects then have no DDIC edges, and their DTEL / DOMA show `no-evidence`.

`build-package-graph` (G5) merges `ddic-reads.json`, `ddic.json` and `ddic-facts.md`. Its summary line names G3a reads that failed or were truncated (`ddicReads`).

## G4 — Usage (main thread, ECC only)

`<SAPV>` = `ECC` and the tools exist:

- `GetTcodeUsage` with every TRAN member (months 12) → the result as `tcodes`.
- `GetJobUsage` with every PROG member (months 12) → the result as `jobs`.

Write `<DIR>/usage.json` = `{ "system": <SAP system id>, "measuredAt": <today>, "tcodes": …, "jobs": … }` (results unchanged). Either call fails → leave that key out. S/4 or neither tool available → no `usage.json`. The graph is still built, and finalize skips the usage section.

### G4u — Usage from another system (QA / PRD)

A DEV profile (`config.json → tier` = `DEV`) measures developer tests, not business use. The destination is site-specific: every installation names its own — never assume one. Read `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST` from the profile `sap.env`.

- **Set** → G4 calls `GetTcodeUsage` with `destination: "<SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST>"` (passed explicitly, so a just-edited `sap.env` works without a restart). The result's `system` is the measured SID → write it as `tcodes.source = { system, destination, kind: "rfc" }`. `GetJobUsage` stays on the connected system — say so in the progress line. A call error (`RFC destination … failed`, missing authorization) → print it and fall through to the question below.
- **Not set** on a DEV profile → ask once (any SAP version — the file path works on S/4 too): `Read QA / PRD over RFC (Recommended)` / `Submit QA / PRD used TCodes (file)` / `Use <SAP system id> statistics` / `Skip usage`.
  - RFC → ask for the SM59 destination name (on the connected system, pointing to QA / PRD); prerequisites: the destination's user needs `S_RFC` for function groups `SWNC_COLLECTOR` + `SRFC` and workload read authorization (`S_TOOLS_EX`). Call once; success → offer to save it as `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST` via `/sc4sap:sap-option` (one line, no auto-write).
  - File → the export recipe below.

Submitted file: print the export recipe, then take a file path or a pasted list:

```
QA/PRD → ST03N → Expert mode → Workload: Total → Month (pick the months) → Transaction Profile → Standard
→ Transaction tab → List → Export → Spreadsheet (.xlsx) or Local file (unconverted .txt).
Or paste TCode names here (any separator). Jobs (optional): SM37 list of program names, same way.
Window: how many months does the export cover?
```

A pasted list → write it to `<DIR>/usage-input-tcodes.txt` (Write tool) first. Then (main thread, one Bash call per kind):

```bash
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/import-usage.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --file "<file>" --system <QA SID> --months <n> [--kind jobs]
```

It keeps only package members, sets every member absent from the file to `false`, records `source` (system, file, date), and prints `{ kind, members, used, notInPackage }`. Exit 2 = no package member in the file → show the message, ask once for another file, else continue without usage. `notInPackage` > 0 is normal (other packages' TCodes) — print the count only. Submitted TCodes + live `GetJobUsage` may be combined; the usage result names each source in its caveats. Resume: an imported side (`source.kind` = `user-file`) is reused like a measured one (≤ 7 days).

## G5 — Build (main thread, one Bash call)

```bash
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/build-package-graph.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --src "<SRC>" --system <SAP system id> --sap-version <SAPV>
```

It prints one JSON line `{ graph, nodes, edges, unresolved, sourcesMissing, usage?, fields? }` and writes `<DIR>/graph.json` (+ `usage-result.json`, `usage.md` when `usage.json` exists; `fields.json` — field-level CRUD for the relation map's Fields tab — when G3a read DD03L). Exit code ≠ 0 → print the stderr line and continue to Step D without a graph (finalize falls back to the scout facts). Do not read the JSON files into the main context. Finalize reads them.

Progress line after G5: `↳ G graph <nodes> nodes · <edges> edges · used <direct>+<indirect> · unused <unused>` (+ ` · fields <refs> refs` when `fields` is present).

## G6 — Customer appends of standard tables (G3a callers only, after G5)

The Fields tab also lists the customer fields appended to the standard tables the package reads or writes (VBAK-ZZ…, CI_ includes). Two small DD03L rounds, same checker contract and hook approval as G3a; skip G6 when G1 parsed no source (no `reads` / `writes` in the graph) or `GetSqlQuery` is not allowed.

```bash
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --only appends --out "<DIR>/ddic-append-plan.json"
# checkers on ddic-append-plan.json (MODE: dd-read) → then:
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>" --plan ddic-append-plan.json --out ddic-appends.json
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --only append-fields --out "<DIR>/ddic-append-fields-plan.json"
# checkers on ddic-append-fields-plan.json → then:
node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>" --plan ddic-append-fields-plan.json --out ddic-append-fields.json
```

`statements` = 0 in either round → stop G6 there (no standard table read, or no customer append). Then rerun G5 — it merges both files into `fields.json`. A failed round only loses the append fields; never fall back to G3b for it. Resume: both files ≤ 7 days old are reused.

## What finalize does with it

Spec: [`../../agents/sap-stocker.md`](../../agents/sap-stocker.md) § Dispatch_Modes → `MODE: finalize`. In short:

- `ref_count` per member = incoming edges in `graph.json` from other members, excluding `include` (`graph-query.mjs <graph.json> stats` → `degree[].in`). This replaces `n/a (ECC …)`.
- `inventory.json → objects[].usage` = `direct` / `indirect` / `unused` / `no-evidence` from `usage-result.json`. `inventory.json → usage` = `{ window, counts, caveats }`.
- `index.md` gets a **Usage** section: counts, the window caveats verbatim, and direct + unused lists. `no-evidence` is never called unused.

Resume: `tcodes.json` / `ddic-reads.json` + `ddic-facts.md` / `usage.json` in `<DIR>` that are ≤ 7 days old are reused (skip G2 / G3 / G4). G5 always reruns — it takes seconds.

# CBO Stocking — Walk, Haiku Scout Fan-out, Finalize

Shared by [`workflow-steps.md`](workflow-steps.md) (stock-cbo Step 3–7). The per-object `GetWhereUsed` graph — one call per package object — moves from one Sonnet stocker working serially to Haiku `sap-checker` workers running in parallel. The stocker keeps every judgment: tiering, business purpose, cross-module gaps, sensitive names, persistence. Model rationale: [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Tier 3 and § Checker fan-out in other skills.

`<DIR>` = the **absolute** directory of the `path=` in the stocker's `WALKED` line. The stocker resolves it per [`../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`](../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md), so it may be under `.sc4sap/work/<alias>/cbo/…` rather than `.sc4sap/cbo/…` — never rebuild it by hand.

`<SAPV>` = `sapVersion` from the active profile's `config.json` (`~/.sc4sap/profiles/<alias>/config.json`, legacy `.sc4sap/config.json`), read by the main thread before Step A. **ECC mode** (`<SAPV>` = `ECC`): `GetWhereUsed` returns ADT 404 for programs and tables on ECC, so no dispatch in this flow calls it — scouts write `callers` as `n/a (ECC — where-used unavailable)` and finalize scores from the source / DDIC reference graph built in Step G.

## Step A — Walk (`sc4sap:sap-stocker`, `MODE: walk`)

Banner: `▶ phase=walk (stocker) · agent=sap-stocker · model=Sonnet`. The `MODE:` line must be the prompt's first line; caller-specific text goes after it.

```
MODE: walk
Package <PACKAGE> (module <MODULE>, SAP version <SAPV>). Flagship programs: <KEY_PROGRAMS or "none">.
Run Investigation_Protocol steps 1–2 only, write walk.json, return the WALKED line.
```

The stocker returns one line: `WALKED objects=<n> batches=<b> path=<absolute path of walk.json>`. `BLOCKED: <reason>` → re-dispatch once with `model: "opus"` and the blocker context ([`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Escalation pattern); still blocked → surface and stop.

**Walk reuse (optional, caller-enabled):** when the active-profile inventory directory already holds a `walk.json` for the same package that is ≤ 7 days old, the caller may skip this dispatch and take `objects` / `batches` from that file (`<DIR>` = its directory). A `scout-facts.md` there with one `CHECKER … END` block per batch also skips Step C; a partial one → run Step C for the missing batches only and append.

## Step B — Gate

- `objects < 30` → skip Step C. Dispatch Step D without a facts file; the stocker runs step 3 (graph) itself as before (ECC mode: no graph — see Step D).
- `objects ≥ 30` → main reads `walk.json → batches[]` (`NAME:TYPE` strings only) and runs Step C.

## Step C — Scout fan-out (`sc4sap:sap-checker` × `batches`, `MODE: scout`)

One checker per batch (20 objects each; the stocker widens batches so there are at most 16). **At most 8 checkers per message** (one ADT session serves them all): batches 1–8 in the first message, the rest in a second message after the first returns. Banner per message: `▶ phase=scout · agent=sap-checker×<n> · model=Haiku`.

```
MODE: scout
Objects (your whole scope): <NAME:TYPE, NAME:TYPE, …>          ← main inlines the batch
Package member list: <DIR>/walk.json → objects[]  (Read it; use it ONLY to filter callers — every object
  in your scope is a package member: fetch all of them, never drop one as "not in package")
Flagship programs: <KEY_PROGRAMS or "none">
For each object return:
- key="callers" value="in_pkg=<n> names=<up to 10 in-package caller names> flagship=<flagship names or ->"
  — GetWhereUsed once. Compute flagship= from the full caller list FIRST, then keep only callers whose
    name is in objects[] for in_pkg / names.
  — DTEL / DOMA: no callers line and no GetWhereUsed (their where-used lists are huge and add no signal).
  — ECC mode: the main thread replaces this whole bullet with:
    key="callers" value="n/a (ECC — where-used unavailable)" for every object — do NOT call GetWhereUsed.
- key="ddic" value="<short text + key fields (TABL / VIEW) | component count (STRU / TTYP) |
  domain + length (DTEL / DOMA) | FM list (FUGR) | first method or signature head (CLAS / INTF / FUNC) | title (PROG)>"
  — the matching Get* tool; object types you have no tool for (DDLS, BDEF, SRVD, SRVB, …) → value="-".
  — INCL / TRAN / PARA (and any other type not listed above) → value="-" without a fetch; never read include source.
- key="lines" value="<n>" — flagship PROG only: GetProgFullCode with output: "file", count from the outline.
  No lines fact for any other object.

1	# CBO Stocking — Step G: Reference Graph + Usage
2	
3	Runs between Step C (scouts) and Step D (finalize) of [`stocker-fanout.md`](stocker-fanout.md), for both callers (`stock-cbo`). It builds `graph.json` (who calls / includes / submits / reads / writes / types what, from source; how the DDIC objects relate — typing, check tables, search helps, value tables, row types, view bases — from DDIC) and, on ECC, `usage-result.json` (which members are actually used). Finalize then ranks from the graph instead of `GetWhereUsed`, which returns 404 on ECC.
4	
5	`<DIR>` = the inventory directory from the `WALKED` line. `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` = the folder that holds `skills/`, `scripts/`, `common/` (two levels above this skill's `SKILL.md`, or `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`); quote it in shell commands. `<SAPV>` = `ECC` or `S4` as in `stocker-fanout.md`.
6	
7	Banner: `▶ phase=graph · agent=main · batch reads`. Every sub-step is mechanical — no judgment, so no Sonnet / Opus dispatch here. G1, G1b and G3a run as **batch reads on the main thread**: `scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs` writes the plan, `scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs` runs it in one process (read tools only; DD-shaped `GetSqlQuery` only) and prints one line per call — `<id>⇥OK⇥<value>` or `<id>⇥ERROR⇥<message>`. Results stay on disk; never Read the sources or the SQL results. Batch fallback: when `sap-batch` fails as a whole (`sap-batch: <error>`, exit ≠ 0 — the bridge did not start), print `↳ batch reads unavailable: <error>` and run the same scope with `sc4sap:sap-checker` (`MODE: scout`, 10 objects per checker, at most 8 per message, one line per object `key="src" value="<folder>"` / `value="ERROR <message>"`, never read the source).
8	
9	## G1 — Fetch sources (main thread, batch)
10	
11	Scope = every `PROG/P` and `FUGR` in `walk.json → objects[]` (`PROG/I` members are includes: read through their owner, or in G1b). `calls` = 0 → skip.
12	
13	```bash
14	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --sources "<DIR>/walk.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-src.json"
15	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-src.json"
16	```
17	
18	Callers that keep sources between runs add `--skip-present "<SRC>"` to the first command (member folders already on disk are not fetched again). More than 150 calls → run the plan in parts, `--from 1 --to 150`, `--from 151 --to 300`, … (one Bash call each; a part takes about two minutes). `OK` lines carry the member folder (`GetProgFullCode` `output: "file"`, ends in `.prog` / `.fugr`). `<SRC>` = their parent directory (one MCP output directory). `ERROR` lines are not retried — `build-package-graph` lists those objects under `sourcesMissing`, and finalize names them in `index.md`.
19	
20	### G1b — Includes no member program pulls in
21	
22	Package includes no G1 folder holds: user-exit includes (included by SAP programs such as `MV45AFZZ`), leftovers, and includes a member program pulls in that its `GetProgFullCode` folder came back without:
23	
24	```bash
25	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/build-package-graph.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --src "<SRC>" --orphans > "<DIR>/orphans.json"
26	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --orphans "<DIR>/orphans.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-incl.json"
27	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-incl.json"
28	```
29	
30	`calls` = 0 → skip the last command. The files land in `<SRC>` as `<name>.incl.abap`. G5 joins an include to the member program whose source has `INCLUDE <name>`; the others become objects of their own. Its summary reports what is still missing under `orphanIncludes`.
31	
32	## G2 — TCodes (main thread)
33	
34	TRAN members → one `GetTransaction` call with `transaction_names: [...]` (batches of 100). Save the JSON result unchanged as `<DIR>/tcodes.json`. It maps report / dialog TCodes to their program and parameter TCodes (SM30) to their view. A failed call → write `[]` and add `TCode mapping unavailable: <message>` to the finalize prompt.
35	
36	## G3 — DDIC relations
37	
38	Two ways in. G3a reads the DD repository tables once per table kind. G3b is the per-object checker read: it is the fallback for what G3a could not read, and the only way for callers that do not allow `GetSqlQuery` (`module-to-process`). Edge kinds: `types` (field → DTEL, `.INCLUDE` / `.APPEND` → STRU, DTEL → DOMA), `checks` (field → check table, with cardinality), `searchHelp`, `valueTable`, `rowType`, `basedOn` (view → base table), `selects` (search help → selection method), `contains` (collective search help). Only customer (Z / Y / namespace) targets and members become nodes.
39	
40	### G3a — DD reads (main thread, batch; stock-cbo only)
41	
42	The one exception to "no `GetSqlQuery`" in this skill: **DD\* repository tables and repository short-text tables only** — the statements in the plan file, nothing else, never `acknowledge_risk`. They are metadata about the package's DDIC objects, never business rows. The `permission-approver` hook auto-approves these statements (`output: "file"` is part of the match — never drop it); any other form prompts. Neither the SQL text nor the results pass through the main thread.
43	
44	```bash
45	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --lang <SAP_LANGUAGE> --out "<DIR>/ddic-plan.json"
46	```
47	
48	It writes the plan (DD03L, DD08L, DD05S, DD35L, DD04L, DD01L, DD40L, DD26S, DD30L, DD31S — single-table `SELECT … WHERE … IN (…)`; S4 packs 200 names per statement, ECC 50 because the `TABLE_READ` condition travels in a URL), plus the object short texts in the logon language and English (DD02T, DD04T, DD01T, DD40T, DD30T, DD25T, TRDIRT, TSTCT, TFTIT, TLIBT, SEOCLASSTX — repository texts, never business rows; the relation map shows them as descriptions). On ECC, names containing `SELECT` or `JOIN` are left out: `TABLE_READ` refuses any condition with those words, literals included. It prints `{ plan, statements, slices: [{ from, to }] }`. `statements` = 0 → no DDIC members; skip G3. Otherwise run every statement as one batch (`sap-batch` refuses any statement that is not in the DD shape the hook auto-approves):
49	
50	```bash
51	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/fetch-plan.mjs" --ddic "<DIR>/ddic-plan.json" --out "<DIR>/fetch-dd.json"
52	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/lib/sap-batch.mjs" --plan "<DIR>/fetch-dd.json"
53	```
54	
55	Batch fallback (see the banner note): one `sap-checker` per slice, `MODE: dd-read`, prompt `Plan file: <DIR>/ddic-plan.json — run entries <from>–<to> (1-based, in order). For each entry call GetSqlQuery { sql_query: <entry.sql>, row_number: <entry.row_number>, output: "file" }.`
56	
57	Then (main thread, one Bash call; `<SQLDIR>` = the `sql` folder of the MCP output directory, next to `<SRC>` — `<PROJECT>/.sc4sap/work/<alias>/mcp-output/sql`):
58	
59	```bash
60	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>"
61	```
62	
63	It matches each plan entry to its result file by exact SQL text and writes `<DIR>/ddic-reads.json` (`{ id, table, path, rows, truncated }` or `{ id, table, error }`), printing `{ reads, ok, errors, truncated }`. Batch `ERROR` lines (or checker `RUN … result=error` lines) are only for the progress line.
64	
65	G3b then covers the gaps: a `dd03l-*` read failed or truncated → the tables of that statement; a `DD04L` / `DD01L` / `DD40L` / `DD26S` read failed → the DTEL / DOMA / TTYP / VIEW members of that statement. A failed `DD08L` / `DD05S` / `DD35L` / `DD30L` / `DD31S` read only loses cardinality or search help detail — no G3b for it. No result file was written (MCP server older than 4.8.19 ignores `output`; a fallback checker reports `result=inline`) → G3b for the whole scope; same when every read failed with the same error — print `↳ G3a DD reads unavailable: <error>`. On ECC an `is not allowed` error means the system's `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` predates the DD allow list (reinstall via `/sc4sap:setup`).
66	
67	### G3b — Per-object reads (`sc4sap:sap-checker` × n, `MODE: scout`)
68	
69	DDIC metadata only (`GetTable` / `GetStructure` / `GetDataElement` / `GetDomain` / `GetTypeInfo`) — never `GetSqlQuery` / `GetTableContents`. Scope = the members G3a did not cover, 20 per checker, at most 8 checkers per message. It can share a message with G1.
70	
71	```
72	MODE: scout
73	Objects (your whole scope): <NAME:TABL, NAME:STRU, NAME:DTEL, NAME:DOMA, NAME:TTYP, …>
74	For each object, one read; lines only for customer targets (name starts with Z or Y, or a /namespace/):
75	- TABL / STRU: GetTable (TABL) or GetStructure (STRU). Per field with a customer rollname or domname:
76	  key="types" value="<FIELDNAME>=<ROLLNAME>/<DOMNAME>" (no domname → "<FIELDNAME>=<ROLLNAME>").
77	  Per customer check table (field checktable, or DDL "with foreign key <TAB>"): key="check" value="<FIELDNAME>=<TAB>".
78	  Per included structure (.INCLUDE / .APPEND row precfield, or DDL "include <STRU>"): key="include" value="<STRU>".
79	  Per field search help (field shlpname, or DDL "with value help <SHLP>"): key="shlp" value="<FIELDNAME>=<SHLP>".
80	- DTEL: GetDataElement → key="domain" value="<DOMNAME or ->"; search help set → key="shlp" value="<SHLP>".
81	- DOMA: GetDomain → value table set → key="valtab" value="<TAB>".
82	- TTYP: S/4 only — GetTypeInfo → row type → key="rowtype" value="<ROWTYPE>". On ECC no line.
83	A field the answer does not have (older ECC bridge) gives no line — never guess.
84	```
85	
86	Main writes every `CHECKER … END` block unchanged to `<DIR>/ddic-facts.md` (malformed block → repair once per `../../common/structured-return-repair.md`). A `BLOCKED` batch is not retried. Its objects then have no DDIC edges, and their DTEL / DOMA show `no-evidence`.
87	
88	`build-package-graph` (G5) merges `ddic-reads.json`, `ddic.json` and `ddic-facts.md`. Its summary line names G3a reads that failed or were truncated (`ddicReads`).
89	
90	## G4 — Usage (main thread, ECC only)
91	
92	`<SAPV>` = `ECC` and the tools exist:
93	
94	- `GetTcodeUsage` with every TRAN member (months 12) → the result as `tcodes`.
95	- `GetJobUsage` with every PROG member (months 12) → the result as `jobs`.
96	
97	Write `<DIR>/usage.json` = `{ "system": <SAP system id>, "measuredAt": <today>, "tcodes": …, "jobs": … }` (results unchanged). Either call fails → leave that key out. S/4 or neither tool available → no `usage.json`. The graph is still built, and finalize skips the usage section.
98	
99	### G4u — Usage from another system (QA / PRD)
100	
101	A DEV profile (`config.json → tier` = `DEV`) measures developer tests, not business use. The destination is site-specific: every installation names its own — never assume one. Read `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST` from the profile `sap.env`.
102	
103	- **Set** → G4 calls `GetTcodeUsage` with `destination: "<SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST>"` (passed explicitly, so a just-edited `sap.env` works without a restart). The result's `system` is the measured SID → write it as `tcodes.source = { system, destination, kind: "rfc" }`. `GetJobUsage` stays on the connected system — say so in the progress line. A call error (`RFC destination … failed`, missing authorization) → print it and fall through to the question below.
104	- **Not set** on a DEV profile → ask once (any SAP version — the file path works on S/4 too): `Read QA / PRD over RFC (Recommended)` / `Submit QA / PRD used TCodes (file)` / `Use <SAP system id> statistics` / `Skip usage`.
105	  - RFC → ask for the SM59 destination name (on the connected system, pointing to QA / PRD); prerequisites: the destination's user needs `S_RFC` for function groups `SWNC_COLLECTOR` + `SRFC` and workload read authorization (`S_TOOLS_EX`). Call once; success → offer to save it as `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST` via `/sc4sap:sap-option` (one line, no auto-write).
106	  - File → the export recipe below.
107	
108	Submitted file: print the export recipe, then take a file path or a pasted list:
109	
110	```
111	QA/PRD → ST03N → Expert mode → Workload: Total → Month (pick the months) → Transaction Profile → Standard
112	→ Transaction tab → List → Export → Spreadsheet (.xlsx) or Local file (unconverted .txt).
113	Or paste TCode names here (any separator). Jobs (optional): SM37 list of program names, same way.
114	Window: how many months does the export cover?
115	```
116	
117	A pasted list → write it to `<DIR>/usage-input-tcodes.txt` (Write tool) first. Then (main thread, one Bash call per kind):
118	
119	```bash
120	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/import-usage.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --file "<file>" --system <QA SID> --months <n> [--kind jobs]
121	```
122	
123	It keeps only package members, sets every member absent from the file to `false`, records `source` (system, file, date), and prints `{ kind, members, used, notInPackage }`. Exit 2 = no package member in the file → show the message, ask once for another file, else continue without usage. `notInPackage` > 0 is normal (other packages' TCodes) — print the count only. Submitted TCodes + live `GetJobUsage` may be combined; the usage result names each source in its caveats. Resume: an imported side (`source.kind` = `user-file`) is reused like a measured one (≤ 7 days).
124	
125	## G5 — Build (main thread, one Bash call)
126	
127	```bash
128	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/build-package-graph.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --src "<SRC>" --system <SAP system id> --sap-version <SAPV>
129	```
130	
131	It prints one JSON line `{ graph, nodes, edges, unresolved, sourcesMissing, usage?, fields? }` and writes `<DIR>/graph.json` (+ `usage-result.json`, `usage.md` when `usage.json` exists; `fields.json` — field-level CRUD for the relation map's Fields tab — when G3a read DD03L). Exit code ≠ 0 → print the stderr line and continue to Step D without a graph (finalize falls back to the scout facts). Do not read the JSON files into the main context. Finalize reads them.
132	
133	Progress line after G5: `↳ G graph <nodes> nodes · <edges> edges · used <direct>+<indirect> · unused <unused>` (+ ` · fields <refs> refs` when `fields` is present).
134	
135	## G6 — Customer appends of standard tables (G3a callers only, after G5)
136	
137	The Fields tab also lists the customer fields appended to the standard tables the package reads or writes (VBAK-ZZ…, CI_ includes). Two small DD03L rounds, same checker contract and hook approval as G3a; skip G6 when G1 parsed no source (no `reads` / `writes` in the graph) or `GetSqlQuery` is not allowed.
138	
139	```bash
140	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --only appends --out "<DIR>/ddic-append-plan.json"
141	# checkers on ddic-append-plan.json (MODE: dd-read) → then:
142	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>" --plan ddic-append-plan.json --out ddic-appends.json
143	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/ddic-queries.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sap-version <SAPV> --only append-fields --out "<DIR>/ddic-append-fields-plan.json"
144	# checkers on ddic-append-fields-plan.json → then:
145	node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/graph/collect-ddic-reads.mjs" --dir "<DIR>" --sql-dir "<SQLDIR>" --plan ddic-append-fields-plan.json --out ddic-append-fields.json
146	```
147	
148	`statements` = 0 in either round → stop G6 there (no standard table read, or no customer append). Then rerun G5 — it merges both files into `fields.json`. A failed round only loses the append fields; never fall back to G3b for it. Resume: both files ≤ 7 days old are reused.
149	
150	## What finalize does with it
151	
152	Spec: [`../../agents/sap-stocker.md`](../../agents/sap-stocker.md) § Dispatch_Modes → `MODE: finalize`. In short:
153	
154	- `ref_count` per member = incoming edges in `graph.json` from other members, excluding `include` (`graph-query.mjs <graph.json> stats` → `degree[].in`). This replaces `n/a (ECC …)`.
155	- `inventory.json → objects[].usage` = `direct` / `indirect` / `unused` / `no-evidence` from `usage-result.json`. `inventory.json → usage` = `{ window, counts, caveats }`.
156	- `index.md` gets a **Usage** section: counts, the window caveats verbatim, and direct + unused lists. `no-evidence` is never called unused.
157	
158	Resume: `tcodes.json` / `ddic-reads.json` + `ddic-facts.md` / `usage.json` in `<DIR>` that are ≤ 7 days old are reused (skip G2 / G3 / G4). G5 always reruns — it takes seconds.

# CBO Stocking — Walk, Haiku Scout Fan-out, Finalize

Shared by [`workflow-steps.md`](workflow-steps.md) (stock-cbo Step 3–7). The per-object `GetWhereUsed` graph — one call per package object — moves from one Sonnet stocker working serially to Haiku `sap-checker` workers running in parallel. The stocker keeps every judgment: tiering, business purpose, cross-module gaps, sensitive names, persistence. Model rationale: [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Tier 3 and § Checker fan-out in other skills.

`<DIR>` = the **absolute** directory of the `path=` in the stocker's `WALKED` line. The stocker resolves it per [`../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`](../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md), so it may be under `.sc4sap/work/<alias>/cbo/…` rather than `.sc4sap/cbo/…` — never rebuild it by hand.

`<SAPV>` = `sapVersion` from the active profile's `config.json` (`~/.sc4sap/profiles/<alias>/config.json`, legacy `.sc4sap/config.json`), read by the main thread before Step A. **ECC mode** (`<SAPV>` = `ECC`): `GetWhereUsed` returns ADT 404 for programs and tables on ECC, so no dispatch in this flow calls it — scouts write `callers` as `n/a (ECC — where-used unavailable)` and finalize scores from the source / DDIC reference graph built in Step G.

## Step A — Walk (`sc4sap:sap-stocker`, `MODE: walk`)

Banner: `▶ phase=walk (stocker) · agent=sap-stocker · model=Sonnet`. The `MODE:` line must be the prompt's first line; caller-specific text goes after it.

```
MODE: walk
Package <PACKAGE> (module <MODULE>, SAP version <SAPV>). Flagship programs: <KEY_PROGRAMS or "none">.
Run Investigation_Protocol steps 1–2 only, write walk.json, return the WALKED line.
```

The stocker returns one line: `WALKED objects=<n> batches=<b> path=<absolute path of walk.json>`. `BLOCKED: <reason>` → re-dispatch once with `model: "opus"` and the blocker context ([`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Escalation pattern); still blocked → surface and stop.

**Walk reuse (optional, caller-enabled):** when the active-profile inventory directory already holds a `walk.json` for the same package that is ≤ 7 days old, the caller may skip this dispatch and take `objects` / `batches` from that file (`<DIR>` = its directory). A `scout-facts.md` there with one `CHECKER … END` block per batch also skips Step C; a partial one → run Step C for the missing batches only and append.

## Step B — Gate

- `objects < 30` → skip Step C. Dispatch Step D without a facts file; the stocker runs step 3 (graph) itself as before (ECC mode: no graph — see Step D).
- `objects ≥ 30` → main reads `walk.json → batches[]` (`NAME:TYPE` strings only) and runs Step C.

## Step C — Scout fan-out (`sc4sap:sap-checker` × `batches`, `MODE: scout`)

One checker per batch (20 objects each; the stocker widens batches so there are at most 16). **At most 8 checkers per message** (one ADT session serves them all): batches 1–8 in the first message, the rest in a second message after the first returns. Banner per message: `▶ phase=scout · agent=sap-checker×<n> · model=Haiku`.

```
MODE: scout
Objects (your whole scope): <NAME:TYPE, NAME:TYPE, …>          ← main inlines the batch
Package member list: <DIR>/walk.json → objects[]  (Read it; use it ONLY to filter callers — every object
  in your scope is a package member: fetch all of them, never drop one as "not in package")
Flagship programs: <KEY_PROGRAMS or "none">
For each object return:
- key="callers" value="in_pkg=<n> names=<up to 10 in-package caller names> flagship=<flagship names or ->"
  — GetWhereUsed once. Compute flagship= from the full caller list FIRST, then keep only callers whose
    name is in objects[] for in_pkg / names.
  — DTEL / DOMA: no callers line and no GetWhereUsed (their where-used lists are huge and add no signal).
  — ECC mode: the main thread replaces this whole bullet with:
    key="callers" value="n/a (ECC — where-used unavailable)" for every object — do NOT call GetWhereUsed.
- key="ddic" value="<short text + key fields (TABL / VIEW) | component count (STRU / TTYP) |
  domain + length (DTEL / DOMA) | FM list (FUGR) | first method or signature head (CLAS / INTF / FUNC) | title (PROG)>"
  — the matching Get* tool; object types you have no tool for (DDLS, BDEF, SRVD, SRVB, …) → value="-".
  — INCL / TRAN / PARA (and any other type not listed above) → value="-" without a fetch; never read include source.
- key="lines" value="<n>" — flagship PROG only: GetProgFullCode with output: "file", count from the outline.
  No lines fact for any other object.
